channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Aesthetic Dynamics · LoosenArt
item.description: LoosenArt's open call for a new issue of its Issue Collective editorial project, on the theme Aesthetic Dynamics. Entry is free and open worldwide, and the accepted media are stated plainly: photographic, video and digital works are welcome, with no restriction on style or genre. The theme asks for contemporary readings of aesthetic dynamism, a lineage the call traces from the nineteenth-century study of the organic world — when the microscope, X-rays and microphotography opened up dimensions that had been difficult to observe — through Art Nouveau's curved, sinuous lines and fluid forms, and Futurism's speed, movement and simultaneity, to what those ways of seeing can become now. Selected works are brought together inside the publication as a single editorial narrative connecting different contemporary interpretations of the theme. A selection of the works chosen for publication will also be considered for a further selection process leading to a group exhibition to be held in 2027 in one of three cities — Milan, Rome or Cagliari — which the organiser has not yet fixed. Submission is through a Google Form asking for name, country, email, website, Instagram, an artist statement of up to 70 words in English, and up to three image files of no more than 5 MB each, renamed for the work's title. The deadline is 17 October 2026. Be aware that LoosenArt's site is now a spare Google Sites presence run from Quartu Sant'Elena in Sardinia, and beyond the call text itself it publishes no further terms; no charge of any kind is mentioned at any stage, either on the call page or in the entry form. — Deadline: October 17, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Curatorial Research Fellowship 2027 · Les Rencontres d'Arles
item.description: Les Rencontres d'Arles offers a curatorial research fellowship of up to €20,000, open to all exhibition curators, for an unpublished project connected to the image and to photography. It runs in two phases: a period of research around an exhibition project, and then — if the festival validates that research after six months — production of the exhibition itself. The money splits the same way. €5,000 is paid to the winner outright as an author's fee; the remaining €15,000 is conditional on validation and is a production budget steered by the Rencontres, covering loans of works, transport to Arles and back, production of the works (prints, framing, wallpapers, video and so on), the curator's invitation and, where applicable, the artists' costs in Arles during opening week or the installation, and insurance. Scenography, communication, installation, de-installation and invigilation are carried by the festival on top of that budget. In exchange the curator undertakes to select the works making up the exhibition's corpus and settle their presentation and reproduction rights, to conceive and write a presentation text for the selection of photographs, and to be present during the festival's opening week and take part in the guided tour of the exhibition. The application is a single PDF of no more than 10 MB, in the order the organiser specifies: a presentation text for the proposed exhibition project of at most 5,000 characters; the corpus of works and artists envisaged, with visuals strongly recommended; a provisional research budget of €5,000; a research schedule; a provisional production budget of €15,000; and the curator's biography, with training, full contact details and a list of the projects and exhibitions they have realised. Texts may be in French or English, ideally both. Applications opened on 16 September 2026 and close on 30 November 2026; the winning projects are announced at the end of February 2027, the research phase runs to summer 2027, and the study is delivered between September and mid-October 2027, after which production begins if the project is validated. There is no application fee. Note that this is a call for exhibition curators, not a call for photographers to submit their own pictures. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €20,000.

item.title: 2026 Architectural Photography Competition (APC26) · AIA Long Beach/South Bay
item.description: The biennial architectural photography competition of the American Institute of Architects' Long Beach/South Bay chapter, open to photographers as well as architects and designers — the chapter's own announcement invites "photographers, architects, designers, and lovers of the built environment". Entries are accepted 31 August to 31 October 2026 in three categories: Exterior (form, materials, context, light, landscape and the relationship between a building and its surroundings), Interior (composition, materiality, light, scale, detail and the experience of being within a space) and, new for 2026, Regional Focus, for architecture inside the chapter's own Long Beach/South Bay boundaries. All entries automatically qualify for a People's Choice award. Enter one category per image; multiple entries are welcome. The chapter states plainly that judging focuses on the photographic image rather than the architecture itself. No cash prize is published: winners are announced in early December 2026 and asked for a print-quality high-resolution file, and Regional Focus selections may additionally be redrawn as sketches for the 2027 Color Your City architecture coloring book with the photographer credited. In the 2024 edition the chapter published each winning photograph alongside written comments from all three jurors — Nirav Solanki, Janna Ireland and Paul Turang — plus an online gallery of every submission; the 2026 jury has not been announced on either the announcement or the entry guidelines. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: $35 non-members / $25 AIA members / $10 students. Prize: None listed.

item.title: Attraction to Abstraction 2026 · Wayne Art Center
item.description: Wayne Art Center's juried exhibition of abstract work, hung in the Vidinghoff and Radnor Township Galleries outside Philadelphia alongside CraftForms, the centre's 31st International Exhibition of Contemporary Fine Craft. Photography is one of the five media named as eligible — "Painting, Works on Paper, Photography, Mixed Media and Fiber Works" — so this is one of the few regional abstraction shows where lens-based work is explicitly invited. Up to three abstract works may be entered on one application at $25 per piece; each must have been completed since January 2024, must not have been shown at Wayne Art Center before, must be at least 24 inches in each direction including any frame, and must be for sale, with the centre retaining a 40% commission. All accepted work is hand-delivered to and collected from Wayne, Pennsylvania on set dates — nothing is shipped in either direction, with no exceptions. The juror of entry is Vlad Milan Duchev, born in Pokrov, Ukraine in 1965, who trained first in painting at an art school in Bila Tserkva and then as a classical double bassist at the Music College of Zhytomyr, the Music Academy of Kharkiv and the National Conservatory of Ukraine in Kyiv, painting alongside his musical career throughout. Registration runs 22 September to 21 October 2026, notification 31 October, hand delivery 23 November, and the exhibition runs 6 December 2026 to 23 January 2027, opening the evening of 5 December at the CraftForms Preview Party. Note that the two surfaces disagree on scope: the CaFÉ prospectus opens the call to "WAC students, WAC members and regional artists 18 years of age and older" without defining the region, while wayneart.org's exhibition page describes the show as work "by our adult students and WAC community members" in a paragraph that still carries last year's title. — Deadline: October 21, 2026. Fee: $25 per work (up to 3 works). Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Signed, Sealed, Delivered: A Postcard Exhibition & Fundraiser · Albrecht-Kemper Museum of Art
item.description: A free, open postcard show at the Albrecht-Kemper Museum of Art in Saint Joseph, Missouri: artists make original 4 × 6 inch postcard artworks, up to five each, in any medium — so photographic prints, contact prints, cyanotypes and other camera-made work all qualify. Be clear about the bargain before entering: this is a fundraiser. Every postcard is exhibited and then sold for $10 with the proceeds going to the museum, the work is not returned to the artist, and there is no prize. What a photographer gets in exchange is a museum wall from late October through 3 January and a buyer who sees their name on the back — the museum asks that the artist's name go on the reverse only, with accompanying information such as a social media handle or website, so that anyone who buys a card can find more of the work. There is no entry fee and no jurying is announced. Postcards are mailed or dropped off to the museum at 2818 Frederick Avenue, Saint Joseph, MO 64506, marked ATTN: Postcard Exhibition, by 23 October 2026. — Deadline: October 23, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: The Present of Presence: Live the Moment · Cape Cod Museum of Art
item.description: The Cape Cod Museum of Art's annual members' juried exhibition, held at the museum's building on Hope Lane in Dennis, Massachusetts. The brief is about attention: in a world of relentless headlines, buzzing devices and climate anxiety, the museum asks what it means to truly inhabit this moment — to see, listen, feel, notice and connect without reaching for the next distraction. Work might celebrate a fleeting encounter, reveal something overlooked, embrace stillness, or capture the intensity of being alive in an uncertain world. Photography is named first in the museum's own list of what will be considered: photography, printmaking, textile, multi-media and three-dimensional artwork. The exhibition is open only to CCMoA members, but membership is bought at the point of entry rather than earned — the call says outright "Not yet a Member of the Cape Cod Museum of Art? You can join today to enter!", and membership runs $30 for students, $50 individual and $85 dual/family, purchasable online. It must stay current through 31 March 2027. Members may submit up to five artworks at $20 for the first and $10 for each additional one, plus a ticket service fee of $0.50 on the first entry and $0.25 on each additional one added at checkout; entry fees are non-refundable. Work must be original, new to CCMoA and not previously exhibited there; any prints must be limited edition and signed. There are no size limits — scale is decided by gallery space. Work arrives framed or on gallery-wrapped canvas at least 1.5 inches deep, ready to hang. AI-generated artwork is not accepted. Juror's Awards of $300, $200 and $100 are presented at the opening reception and gallery talk on Thursday 14 January 2027; the museum has not yet named the juror. Selected artists are notified by end of day on 17 December 2026 and the exhibition runs 8 January to 21 March 2027; work may optionally be offered for sale, on a 60/40 split in the artist's favour. Entries close at noon Eastern on Monday 14 December 2026. — Deadline: December 14, 2026. Fee: $20 first artwork, $10 each additional. Prize: $300 + Exhibition.

item.title: Devotion — Fall 2026 Online Exhibition · Analog Forever Magazine
item.description: Analog Forever Magazine's Fall 2026 online group exhibition, guest-curated by Laura Barth. The brief asks what we give ourselves to. Devotion takes many forms — sacred or secular, private or communal, quiet or consuming — and the call invites photographers to consider the people, places, practices and beliefs to which we give our attention again and again: tending gardens, caring for bodies, returning to familiar places, repeating gestures, preserving memories, making offerings, keeping vigil. The curator is explicit that devotion has shadows too, and that love can become obsession, faith fanaticism, ritual compulsion; work about the cost of loyalty is as welcome as work about its comforts. Interpretations may be spiritual, romantic, familial, ecological, creative, personal or entirely unexpected. This is an analog call — the magazine asks photographers to explore the theme through film and analog photography. Laura Barth is a lens-based multidisciplinary artist who works through experimental analog photographic processes, particularly Polaroid emulsion lifts, turning memory, spirituality and personal mythology into tactile, emotive images; her work has been shown in galleries and in print in the United States and abroad. Submissions go through a Google Form linked from the call page, and selected work goes live when the online exhibition launches on 30 November 2026. Entries close 1 November 2026. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: 2027 Black Creativity Juried Art Exhibition — General Category · Griffin Museum of Science and Industry
item.description: The 57th edition of Black Creativity, the longest continually running exhibition of African American art in the United States, shown at Chicago's Griffin Museum of Science and Industry since 1970. The General Category is open to professional and emerging Black artists aged 18 and over from anywhere in the United States; a separate Teen Category serves Chicagoland artists aged 14 to 17. The museum's own exhibition page names photography outright in the media it shows, alongside paintings, drawings, fine art prints, sculpture, mixed media and ceramics, and the call's medium line reads simply 'contemporary works created in any visual medium' — video is accommodated too, on monitors the museum provides. Three jurors read the submissions: Eddie Chambers, the Goldabelle McComb Finn Distinguished Professor in Art History at the School of the Art Institute of Chicago; Monica Haslip, founder and executive director of Little Black Pearl; and D.E. Simmons, executive director of Diaspora Rhythms. Awards are $4,000 for Best in Show, $2,750 for second place and $1,500 for third, and award winners also receive two tickets to the 2027 Black Creativity Gala. Entry is $10 for up to four works completed between 2024 and 2026, and jurying is blind — you are asked to strip watermarks, credits and your own name from images and statements before uploading. Work must be original, unsold, and not previously selected for a Black Creativity exhibition; AI-generated work is excluded in those same words. Two-dimensional pieces may not exceed 84 inches in any direction and nothing may weigh more than 70 pounds; the museum cannot install ceiling-hung or projected work. Submissions close 11:59pm CST on 11 October 2026, acceptances go out by 4 November, shipping runs 1–16 December with local drop-off on 18–19 December, and the exhibition runs 18 January to 18 April 2027. — Deadline: October 11, 2026. Fee: $10. Prize: $4,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: Delfina Foundation — Portugal & Lusophone Africa Residency 2027
item.description: A twelve-week, fully funded London residency at Delfina Foundation for contemporary visual artists born in Portugal, Angola, Mozambique, Guinea-Bissau, Cape Verde or São Tomé and Príncipe, run in partnership with the UK branch of the Calouste Gulbenkian Foundation. The residency sits inside Delfina's 'open' summer 2027 season — independent research rather than a set theme — and runs 28 June to 17 September 2027. The package is unusually complete: a return economy flight, UK airport transfers, reimbursement of visa fees where required, a £40-a-day living allowance, a £1,200 materials budget, a London travel pass, and a single bedroom with a desk in the Delfina house, which takes up to eight residents around shared bathrooms, laundry, kitchen, library and dining room. Alongside time and space, the season's programme includes guided visits to museums, galleries, non-profits and artist-run spaces in and beyond London, organised encounters with artists, curators, academics and researchers, and professional development in the form of presentations, crits, portfolio reviews and mentoring. Applicants must be seeking to develop their practice through research, be able to explain how an international residency would serve their career and local networks, and be confident discussing their work in English, since the interview is held in English. Artists currently based in the UK are not eligible. The application is a Cognito form asking for a CV and either a portfolio PDF or a personal website, with your practice described in five keywords and again in fifty words, plus contact details for two professional referees. Duos and collectives are discouraged by the accommodation — Delfina asks that one member represent the group — and the foundation states plainly that it welcomes D/deaf, disabled and neurodivergent applicants and will discuss adapting the residency to access needs. Previous unsuccessful applicants are explicitly encouraged to apply again. Applications close 23:59 BST on Sunday 4 October 2026 and everyone is notified by mid-November. — Deadline: October 4, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Funded residency + £1,200 materials budget.

item.title: In Practice: Annual Juried Exhibition · Foothills Art Center
item.description: Foothills Art Center in Golden, Colorado has run an annual Members' Exhibition for over a decade; this year it is renamed In Practice and, for the first time, membership is no longer required to apply. The centre frames the change around its own argument: there is a place for theory, but exhibiting is where artistic technique and decisions are tested in practice, and an artist's practice is never finished or stagnant. All media are eligible, including alternative media — the organiser's phrasing, with no exclusions attached — and work must be original, not previously shown at Foothills, and ready to hang or install. There is no size restriction, though larger works are assessed on whether they use scale effectively. You may enter up to three works and a maximum of one will be selected. New this year are sponsored cash prizes in four categories: $500 for Overall Outstanding Creation, $300 for Mastery of Medium, $300 for Exceptional Originality, and $300 for Viewer's Choice, whose winner is also invited to juror the 2028 edition. The jury is Foothills staff together with Lee Gilliland, the 2026 Viewer's Choice winner, scoring against a published rubric that weights originality of content at 20% and use of media, rendering of subject, colour and contrast, overall concept and composition at 15% each. One caution: the fee is stated twice and the two figures differ. CaFÉ's checkout charges $15, while the prospectus body still reads '$20 entry fee' — budget for the higher figure. Foothills members at the Catalyst level and above can email the curator for a code worth 50% off, and the centre notes it has a free entry-level membership tier. The exhibition runs 6 February to 2 May 2027 at the Astor House, where admission is free seven days a week. — Deadline: November 22, 2026. Fee: $15 (prospectus text says $20). Prize: $500 + Exhibition.

item.title: Shades of Black · Artspiration Frederick
item.description: A juried exhibition for Black History Month at Artspiration Frederick, the non-profit gallery and community art space on Toll House Avenue in Frederick, Maryland, on view 5 to 28 February 2027 with an opening reception on 13 February. Eligibility is reserved for artists who self-identify as Black and/or of African descent, and the organiser is explicit about why: the show exists to give Black artists a dedicated platform, and work does not have to address Black history or identity at all. The subtitle is A Celebration of History. A Vision for the Future, and the framing is that Black art cannot be defined by a single subject, style, history or experience — artists across mediums, generations and career stages are invited on equal terms. All media are welcome and photography is named outright alongside 2D, 3D, ceramics, sculpture and mixed media. Entry is $35 for up to three original works, submitted through CaFÉ with high-resolution 300 dpi files; two-dimensional work must be framed and wired, with sawtooth hangers refused outright. All work must be for sale, with 60% to the artist and 40% to Artspiration, and prices are locked once a piece is entered. The call is open to visual artists 18 and over residing in the continental United States. The juror is not yet named. Accepted artists are notified on 21 January 2027, drop-off runs 31 January to 2 February with shipped work due by 1 February, and pick-up is 28 February or 1–2 March; unretrieved work incurs a $50-a-day storage charge after fourteen days, so read the return-shipping terms before you send anything. Admission to the gallery is free and the space is accessible. — Deadline: January 15, 2027. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Positive Correlations · Cape Cod Museum of Art
item.description: An international juried exhibition for the Hope / McClennen Gallery at the Cape Cod Museum of Art in Dennis, Massachusetts, a museum founded by artists in 1981 and open year-round. The theme is deliberately loose: artists may read Positive Correlations as connections, relationships, patterns, coincidences, evidence, or cause and effect, and the museum says outright that alternative, unexpected and interdisciplinary interpretations are encouraged. The call is open to artists of all ages from the United States and anywhere in the world, and the media list names photography directly — drawing, painting, printmaking, photography, collage, assemblage, sculpture, textiles, multimedia, digital art and video. Photographers get an unusually clear ruling on prints: limited-edition prints and photographic editions are permitted, and digital photography and limited-edition digital printing are acceptable when used to make original photographic work; only reproduction prints of original artworks are refused. AI-generated artwork is not accepted. Each artist may enter up to five works at $25 per work. Two-dimensional pieces must arrive ready to hang, framed or on a gallery-wrapped canvas at least 1.5 inches deep, and Plexiglas is strongly preferred over glass for anything shipped. Work shown previously at the museum is not eligible. Selling is optional rather than a condition of entry; where work does sell, the artist keeps 60%. The juror awards three cash prizes of $500, $200 and $100 — the juror has not yet been named, which is worth weighing before you pay per image. Entries close at midnight Eastern on Monday 8 February 2027, notifications go out by the end of 19 February, delivery and shipped work are due 12 March, and the exhibition runs 19 March to 6 June 2027, with a gallery talk and reception on 26 March. — Deadline: February 8, 2027. Fee: $25 per artwork. Prize: $500 + Exhibition.

item.title: Monochrome · Art Center Sarasota
item.description: The winter juried show in Art Center Sarasota's Atrium Gallery asks for work made in a single colour or a single tonal range. The call frames the constraint as the point: reduction and a limited palette are meant to push bold, nuanced and inventive approaches to value, texture, form and composition, and the organiser notes that subtle shifts in tone and surface can build depth, atmosphere and unexpected complexity. It is open to all artists and all media, and the call names photography explicitly alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, mixed media, digital arts, sculpture and video. AI-generated art is not allowed. The juror is Simone Friend, co-founder of the artist agency Friend & Johnson, who has spent more than forty years representing illustrators, photographers, directors and animators and who is described as drawn to originality, emotional depth, technical mastery and a clear point of view. Jurying is blind — the juror sees everything except the artist's name and the price — and the awards are chosen in person after the exhibition is installed: $500 first place, $300 second, $200 third, plus two merit awards and four honourable mentions. Up to three works may be entered, and a diptych or triptych counts as one. Two-dimensional work may not exceed 72 by 65 inches after framing and three-dimensional work 60 by 36 by 36 inches. Work must be original, completed within the last three years and not previously shown at ACS; editioned prints, including photographs, are allowed if they are labelled as prints and numbered. All work must be offered for sale — no NFS or price-on-request — and the artist receives 60% of the selling price as a member or 50% as a non-member. Artists are notified by 21 December 2026, accepted work is received in person on 12 and 13 January 2027 or by post between 11 and 13 January, and the show runs 21 January to 27 February 2027 with an opening reception on 21 January, 5–7pm. — Deadline: December 13, 2026. Fee: $40 for 1 work, $65 for 3 ($30–$45 members, $10–$35 students). Prize: $500 + Exhibition.

item.title: nice art grant · midwest nice art
item.description: An unrestricted $500 grant from midwest nice art, the artist-run virtual and in-person exhibition project, now in its third cycle. At least two artists are selected each year and the money comes with no strings: the grant supports emerging and mid-career artists to enhance their creative practices, and winners also receive a blog profiling their art and creative practice, a post pinned to the project's profile, and consideration for future jurying and curatorial opportunities — winners are asked to help jury the grant the following year. Additional prizes this cycle include a residency and exhibition with Norse Art Space; shortlisted artists receive automatic acceptance into the annual nice; juried exhibition with a $50 shipping stipend, and semi-finalists get a 50% discount on all future applications for a year. The jury is the organisers Tim Rickett and Epiphany Knedler, previous grant winners hannah smith and noah thomas miller, and Norse Art Space founders Cody Henrichs and Joe Schaeffer. Applicants must be over 18 and located within the United States. The $10 application fee is non-refundable and all applicants must pay it to be considered; midwest nice art says the fees go back into the grant pool and toward further opportunities for artists, including exhibitions, juror fees, education and operating costs. The application asks for a resume or CV and up to five images of the work, submitted as a single PDF labelled FirstInitial_LastName_niceartgrant. Work can be of any medium and subject matter. Applicants hear back with a decision in early spring. — Deadline: January 20, 2027. Fee: $10. Prize: $500 + Residency + Exhibition.

item.title: Development Grants 2026 · Helpmann Academy
item.description: Grants of up to A$3,000 to develop a new idea, build a creative practice or take work further. The Academy designs the funding around six-month projects and names the eligible activities: the creation or realisation of new work or projects, research and development of new ideas, development of new skills in creative practice, a creative or business mentorship, and participation in professional development programmes. Photography is one of nineteen Visual Arts specialisations on the application form, sitting between Installation and Moving Image. Applications are invited from final-year students and graduates of supported degrees at Adelaide University and Flinders University within five years of graduation; honours students and graduates are eligible where the honours study followed directly on from the undergraduate degree, and masters and PhD candidates are not eligible unless they still qualify through earlier study. Funded activity must take place between 1 January and 30 June 2027. The application asks for three written responses of up to 500 words each — your practice to date, a detailed description of the proposal, and why it matters for your career development — plus an artist CV of no more than two pages, an official academic transcript, a project budget on the Academy's template, and four to six images or one to two audio-visual demos; a video submission route is also available. Assessment is on artistic merit, alignment with career development, feasibility and value, potential impact, and capacity to build new networks or collaborations. Applicants are notified within four weeks of the close date. Note that the organiser's own pages disagree by one day: the introductory block on the Apply Now page says applications close Wednesday 30 September, while the same page's KEY DATES footer and the Information for Applicants page both say Tuesday 29 September at 11:59pm ACST. Both dates match their stated weekday, so treat 29 September as the working deadline. Late applications are not accepted. — Deadline: September 29, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: A$3,000.

item.title: Les Boutographies 2027
item.description: Les Boutographies is the European photography festival held every May in Montpellier, created in 2001 and named for a contraction of Boutonnet — the district where it began — and photography. The 2027 edition runs 8 to 30 May and its open call is live from 6 July to 22 November 2026. No theme is set. Anyone resident in Europe may apply, amateur or professional, with no condition of age or nationality, including photographers who have been selected before; applications through an agent are not accepted. Selection runs in stages: the festival's artistic director pre-selects from all entries, then a jury chooses work for hanging or for projection, with the answer given in the applicant's Photographer's Space account, and work not chosen may still be picked up for the Parallèle or Hors les Murs sections. What the festival gives back is unusually concrete. Photographers selected for the exhibition get three nights' accommodation, full coverage of the cost of transporting the work, €100 in author's rights, priority access to the portfolio readings and a place in the festival's book shop with sales remitted in full less card charges; the festival also lists €5,500 for acquisitions alongside production assistance and paid publications, and one work from the official selection is exhibited in Arles during the Rencontres, subject to the partnership being confirmed. Photographers selected for the projection get one night's accommodation, €100 in author's rights and a partner prize of production and an exhibition with the Toulouse lab Photon. Eight prizes are awarded: the Prix du Jury (€1,000 from the festival plus an acquisition by the City of Montpellier worth €2,500, given to a young European photographer whose approach the festival wants to encourage), the Prix du Public (a €500 cheque from Photon toward producing an exhibition, supported by La Gazette de Montpellier), and the Coups de cœur from Réponses Photo (a paid portfolio in the magazine), Photon (a produced exhibition hung for three months in Toulouse), Les Jours (a paid portfolio in the web magazine), The Eyes (two half-days of mentoring), the Jeune Public (honorary, awarded by young Pass Culture members) and Mutuelle des Motards (an acquisition from the official selection for their collection, on the theme the festival gives in English as liberty and support). Entries are 10 to 20 jpgs at 2,000px on the longest side, full-frame with no background except for diptychs, with any captions in a separate Word or PDF list alongside the presentation text; a CV is also required. Registration and payment are on the festival's own site through a photographer's account, which also recovers applications from previous years. — Deadline: November 22, 2026. Fee: €23 per portfolio. Prize: €1,000 + €2,500 acquisition + Exhibition.

item.title: Black Artists Grant (BAG) · Creative Debuts
item.description: A no-strings £500 grant for Black artists based in the UK, awarded monthly by the artist-support platform Creative Debuts. Recipients may spend it on whatever they want — making new work, buying equipment or materials, travel, research, visiting exhibitions or conferences, or simply covering some life expenses — and the grant expects no outcomes and no reporting. Creative Debuts is explicit about why it exists: Black artists are systematically under-supported by the art world, by institutions, curators, the artist-led scene, major and minor funding bodies, the market, art schools and audiences too, and while the organisation says a full institutional overhaul is what is actually required, it hopes the grant helps recipients keep working in the meantime. It currently supports one recipient a month and is sponsored by Creative Debuts itself, whose grants page says more than £130,000 has gone to creatives through the programme. Eligibility is narrow and stated plainly: applicants must be based in the UK and must be Black — the page specifies Black heritage and Black identity, 'not politically Black, not POC or BAME'. There is no age limit and no deadline, since selection is a monthly rolling cycle; apply once only, because all applications are kept and reviewed in later months, and unsuccessful applicants are not notified. One thing to know before applying: the grant is described as open to all creative disciplines, with painters, musicians, directors, jewellers, set designers, sculptors and choreographers given as examples — photography is not among the examples named, and it does not appear on Creative Debuts' grants, featured-artists or open-calls pages either, so a photographer applies under the general all-disciplines wording rather than an explicit invitation. The application form sits on the grant page itself. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: £500.

item.title: America, Beautiful and… · Highfield Hall & Gardens
item.description: A juried exhibition for the United States semiquincentennial at Highfield Hall & Gardens, the restored Beebe family estate in Falmouth on Cape Cod, now a nonprofit cultural centre with a gallery programme. The call asks artists to reflect on the American experience — how America is lived, remembered, celebrated, questioned and reimagined — and the title sets the terms: not only what is beautiful about America, but what comes after the 'and'. The jurors are Jackie Reeves and Lauren Wolk, jointly named the Arts Foundation of Cape Cod's 2026 Artists of the Year and co-founders of The InkLine Project; Wolk is a visual artist represented by Larkin Gallery in Harwich Port and Provincetown as well as a New York Times bestselling author for young readers, a published poet and an award-winning filmmaker, and the organiser frames the pairing as a dialogue between visual art and storytelling. Fine Art Photography is named in the accepted categories, alongside ceramics, collage, drawing, fiber, mixed media, mosaic, oil and acrylic painting, pastel, printmaking, sculpture and watercolour; giclées and similar prints that are copies of original art are not allowed. Awards are $200 for Best in Show, $100 each for four judge's awards, and four honourable mentions. Artists may enter any number of original works — the entry form caps that at twenty — but only one per artist will be accepted and displayed. Work must not have been shown at Highfield before, must be by a living artist and must be made independently rather than under instruction in a class or workshop; the call adds that art must be made from your own photo references and clarifies that no copying of other art is allowed, including art generated by AI — a rule about copy work rather than a ban on AI tools. Two-dimensional work must be framed and wired, with acrylic glazing rather than glass above 30 inches, and work over 40 inches in either direction is less likely to be accepted. Entry costs $20 for the first work and $15 for each after, non-refundable whether or not the work is selected. Files are due by midnight EST on 20 November 2026, acceptances are posted on the Highfield website and emailed between 8 and 11 December, shipped work must arrive by 1 February 2027 with a prepaid return label, hand-delivered work is received on 8 February, and the exhibition runs 4 March to 30 May 2027. Accepted work must stay up for the whole run; withdrawing it brings a two-year ban from Highfield's juried exhibitions. One caution before you apply: Highfield's own website does not publish this call — the source of record is the organiser's own EntryThingy listing, linked below. — Deadline: November 20, 2026. Fee: $20 first entry, $15 each additional. Prize: $200 + Exhibition.

item.title: Celebrating Realism · MVA Gallery
item.description: National call at MVA Gallery (Modern Visual Arts) in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania for work made in the realist tradition. The prospectus traces the thread from Gustave Courbet's Realist Manifesto - everyday people, activities and objects, nature shown with its irregularities, idealised figures and romanticised fantasies rejected - through the twentieth and twenty-first century movements that grew out of it: Photorealism, Social Realism, New Objectivity, American Regionalism and Hyperrealism. The gallery asks how you observe and record perceived reality, how you organise pictorial elements, embrace precision, manipulate light and modify colour tonalities while keeping emotion in the work. There is no restriction on subject matter: landscapes, cityscapes, still lifes, events, special occasions, man-made environments, animals and people are all invited. Artists, photographers and sculptors at every level may enter, all photographic processes are welcome, and there is no cutoff date for when the work was made. Open to US residents aged 18 and over. Entry is $35 for three images and $5 for each additional image up to nine. Jurying is by an anonymous rotating committee of artists, gallerists, art reviewers, publishers and academics. Awards are an Art of Distinction award carrying a featured exhibit in the gallery second room, an optional $200 Director Choice award, honourable mentions that come with free entry to a future MVA show, and an annual grand prize of a New York City exhibition opportunity drawn from everyone shown at the gallery during the year. Work must be wired for hanging, no larger than 48 inches framed and under 50 lbs, sculpture no larger than 28 inches; photographs should be framed in black or white with white or off-white mats if presented traditionally, and plexiglass is preferred over glass for shipped pieces. Accepted work must arrive by 23 February 2027. The gallery takes 30% commission and artists cover shipping and insurance both ways with a prepaid return label. Exhibition runs 28 February to 26 March 2027. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $200 + NYC exhibition.

item.title: 37 Memorial María Luisa
item.description: Long-running international contest for mountain, nature and adventure photography and film, run from Infiesto in Asturias by friends of María Luisa Álvarez, who died in a mountain accident in 1990, and financed by them. The 37th edition has fourteen photographic categories - Mountain Landscape, Alpinism, Climbing, Adventure and Extreme Sports, Man in the Mountain and/or Nature, Animal World, The World of Birds, Vegetal World, Submerged World, Biodiversity and Geodiversity, Nature Landscapes, Creative Photo, Macro Picture, and a Topic of the Year which for this edition is The Universe - plus a category for videos, films and documentaries. For the first time the Memorial also runs a special section for photographers with disabilities. Amateurs and professionals anywhere may enter. The first photograph is free; everything after that is covered by a single €22 payment including VAT that unlocks all categories and the video section, and participation is free for photographers with disabilities and for entrants under 19. Each author may submit up to five photographs per category. Files are JPEG, 1,920 pixels on the longest side, maximum 2 MB, Adobe RGB 1998 preferred, with no frames, borders or captions added; multiple exposure is allowed if registered in camera in a single primary file, and HDR and panoramas are accepted. Judging is anonymous: the system assigns every photograph an alphanumeric code and the panel, drawn by the Founders Board from mountain and nature photographers of recognised prestige, never sees the author. The overall winner takes €5,000, a trophy, a diploma, a book portfolio and two invitations to the awards gala; each of the fourteen category winners takes €300 and the same trophy, diploma, portfolio and invitations. There is a Young Photographers Prize and an Award for the person with a disability, each a Samsung 5G tablet with trophy, diploma, portfolio and invitations, a Citizen watch for the Topic of the Year, and a €3,000 FotoRuano voucher for the best video, film or documentary, with honourable mentions at the panel's discretion. Results are published on 1 March 2027 and the gala is held on 23 and 24 April 2027 in Infiesto and Oviedo, with free accommodation for the winner and a companion. Selected work joins the Memorial's touring exhibition, which is lent framed, labelled and crated to non-profit mountain and environmental organisations. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: First photo free, then €22 for everything else; free for entrants under 19 and for photographers with disabilities. Prize: €5,000 + €300 per category.

item.title: Water: Our Shared Story · Hamdan Bin Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum
item.description: HIPA runs this global competition with the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the 2026 United Nations Water Conference, which the UAE and Senegal co-host in Abu Dhabi from 8 to 10 December 2026. The brief starts from the observation that water is experienced differently across people, communities and environments, and that photography can make those experiences visible - documenting challenges, celebrating solutions and connecting global conversations to real human stories. Entrants submit a story of five to ten photographs exploring the relationship between water and people, communities, the planet, innovation, or challenges. Entry is free and open to individuals aged 18 and over anywhere in the world; submissions run from 16 September to 15 October 2026 at 23:59 UAE time and are made only through the members area of the HIPA site. A title and description for the portfolio are required. Files must be JPEG of at least 5 MB, no less than 2,000 pixels on the longest edge and 300 dpi, and the original RAW or unedited file must be uploaded alongside; phone and drone photographs are allowed. No tags, signatures, initials, frames, borders, logos or other added marks are permitted. Basic technical editing is acceptable so long as it does not affect the authenticity of the photograph, but advanced editing used to create illusions, deceptions or manipulations - including compositing and creative retouching - is prohibited. The prizes are $10,000 for first place, $8,000 for second and $5,000 for third. Winners provide bank and personal details within seven days of request and are paid within two months of the results. Finalists and winners grant HIPA a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free, sub-licensable licence to use the submitted work in connection with the competition and HIPA's own promotion, and entrants must be able to supply model, property and copyright releases on request. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $10,000.

item.title: Dek Unu Magazine — January 2027 Issue
item.description: International not-for-profit journal publishing one accomplished artist per monthly issue in print and online paperback. All fine art projects in all photo genres and techniques are welcome - each feature pairs 11 images with per-image commentary and an in-depth interview, and there is no word limit on the artist's own account of the work. The jurors read the documents as well as the images, and the magazine says it looks for coherent, intentional art, straight to strange, alongside technical excellence. The submission window for the January issue runs November 1-20, 2026, with the magazine closed for jury from the 21st to the 1st of the following month; submissions are by a single email carrying 11 separately named images plus bio and project commentary. Entrants must be at least 18, and submission is limited to artists not previously published by Dek Unu. Dek Unu charges no fee to submit and does not pay contributors; copyright in the images always remains with the artist. — Deadline: November 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Things That Go Bump in the Art · Berkeley Arts Council
item.description: Halloween-themed member exhibit in the back gallery at Berkeley Art Works, the Berkeley Arts Council's space in downtown Martinsburg, West Virginia. The council is calling for artists of the spooky, gothic, medieval, dark, strange and quirky, and says glow-in-the-dark work is especially encouraged. The call does not enumerate media - it asks for artwork rather than naming photography, painting or anything else - but the council's programme is all-media, its annual Eastern West Virginia juried exhibition accepting original two- or three-dimensional work in any medium or technique. Work must be ready to hang and no larger than 24 by 24 inches, with smaller pieces preferred because the back gallery is small; three-dimensional work may be considered if it can be hung or sits on a shelf, and larger pieces may be turned away for lack of space. There is no entry fee and no submission platform: this is a members-only show and work is hand-delivered to the gallery at 116 North Queen Street between 24 and 27 September 2026. Membership can be bought at the point of entry and runs $35 individual, $25 senior and $15 youth or student, with entering exhibitions listed among member benefits. The exhibit runs 1 to 31 October 2026 and culminates in a Halloween reception and costume party on 31 October from 8 to 10 PM, where guests act as judges and vote for a Best Loved award. There is no jury and no cash prize. Proceeds and donations support the council's work connecting artists, audiences and local businesses across Berkeley County. — Deadline: September 27, 2026. Fee: Free (Berkeley Arts Council membership required, from $15). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: The Human Experience · PhotoPlace Gallery
item.description: PhotoPlace Gallery's December call for photographs about the richness, complexity and diversity of human life. Portraits, street photography and documentary work are all welcome, as are pictures about current affairs, family, labour, culture, identity, community and the places we inhabit; the gallery asks for a broad reading of what it means to be human and will take work that is documentary or conceptual, quiet or dramatic, focused directly on people or on the places, events and traces of human presence that tell our stories. Juror Meredith Fleischer, founder of The MF Gallery in Royal Oak, Michigan and Director of The Detroit 15, will select up to 35 photographs for the Middlebury, Vermont gallery and roughly 40 more for the online gallery. All selected work is reproduced in the exhibition book, kept permanently on the PhotoPlace website and promoted through the gallery's publications and social channels; online-gallery selections receive the same catalog inclusion and promotion as the wall selections, and all selected artists are eligible for exhibition awards. Entries opened 7 September 2026 and close 5 October, with juror selections announced 19 October, prints due 20 November and the show running 4-26 December 2026, opening 4 December. There is no limit on the number of images submitted. The gallery's site-wide rules bar fully AI-generated images: all capture methods and photographic techniques are eligible, but submitted work must be created through photographic processes. — Deadline: October 5, 2026. Fee: $39 (5 images) + $6 each additional. Prize: Exhibition + Catalog.

item.title: 2027 Emerging Artist Prize · Cultural Council for Palm Beach County
item.description: A professional-development and recognition programme for visual artists in the early stages of their careers, run by the Cultural Council for Palm Beach County. Five emerging visual artists are selected, each receiving $3,500 in funding for the needs of their practice, four weeks of working studio space at the Norton Museum of Art between June and August 2027, one-to-one mentoring with an established professional in their field, visioning and strategic-planning coaching, group training on the business of an artistic practice, a professional headshot, and recognition in Council press materials and marketing. The programme is built around a cohort of peers at a similar career stage and runs from late January to September 2027. Applicants must live in Palm Beach County at the time of application, identify as an emerging visual artist early in a professional career, and be available for all scheduled in-person and virtual events. Applications open 11 September and close 23 October 2026; panelists meet the week of 16 November, recipients are notified the week of 14 December and announced on 14 January 2027 at the Kruger Family Gallery opening. The call does not enumerate accepted media, but the Council's artist-grant programme does support photographers: its 2026 Artist Innovation Fellows include Quinn Miller, whose funded project is a series of staged photographic compositions. — Deadline: October 23, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $3,500 + Studio residency.

item.title: Handmade · Site:Brooklyn Gallery
item.description: Site:Brooklyn's online juried exhibition on the intelligence of the human hand. The gallery is looking for work across all mediums that foregrounds the artist's hand as both process and subject - the point where thought becomes physical, direct and irreversible action - set against an era increasingly shaped by mechanical and digital reproduction. Juror Pallavi Surana is a New York-based arts writer and curator who has worked on projects with the Kiran Nadar Museum of Art and curator Cecilia Alemani, curated exhibitions at Smack Mellon, GHOSTMACHINE and the Hessel Museum of Art, and written for e-flux Criticism, ARTnews, The Art Newspaper and Ocula; she holds a graduate degree from the Center for Curatorial Studies at Bard College. The call is open to artists 18 and over working in all media, and entries must be original work measured in imperial dimensions. The exhibition runs online from 14 November to 14 December 2026. Entries close 26 October 2026 at 11:59pm MT. — Deadline: October 26, 2026. Fee: $26 (3 images) + $10 each additional. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: Tombstone · Memento Mori Gallery & Tattoo
item.description: Memento Mori's annual Western-adjacent themed group show, timed to the Western Stock Show and, as always at this gallery, opening the door to the outsider, the lowbrow and the macabre. Memento Mori Gallery & Tattoo is a lowbrow/outsider contemporary art space at 6451 W. Colfax Ave in Lakewood, Colorado, in the 40West Arts District and on the First Friday art-walk circuit. Open nationally to 2D and 3D work; up to two pieces per artist at $25 each. Work must be for sale, with a 40% commission to the gallery, and must arrive physically ready to hang or display - hanging hardware already attached, wire preferred, no sawtooth hangers or adhesive mounts. Digital work is only shown if printed and framed or mounted properly. The gallery will not accept photographs of another artist's artwork, including street art, without the artist's express permission to show and sell the photograph. Out-of-state artists cover shipping both ways. Entries close 5 December 2026; drop-off 19 December, show 1-23 January 2027 with a First Friday reception on 1 January, 6-9pm, and pick-up 23 January. — Deadline: December 5, 2026. Fee: $25 per piece. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2027 Members' Juried Exhibition · Tubac Center of the Arts
item.description: Tubac Center of the Arts opens its annual members' juried exhibition to artists across the United States, with all media accepted including video. Members may enter up to three 2D or 3D works completed in the last 24 months and not previously shown at TCA; giclee reproductions are not permitted. Entry is restricted to TCA members, but membership is bought directly from the art centre (Artist and Individual tiers are $50 a year) and is not itself juried - non-members are disqualified without refund, so join before applying. Juror Mary-Beth Buesgen is Lead Curator at the Mesa Contemporary Arts Museum and spent fifteen years at the ASU Art Museum as Curator and Collection Manager of its Ceramics Research Center. Awards total $900 - Best of Show $300, Award of Excellence $200, the Virginia Hall Contemporary Award $100, the Ursula Suess Abstract Award $100, an Award of Merit $100 and two Honorable Mentions at $50 - and are presented at the opening; the awards judge had not been appointed when the call was published and TCA says the prospectus will be updated once one is found. Best of Show also receives a solo exhibit in the Studio Gallery, 2 April - 16 May 2027. Entries open 21 September 2026 and the exhibition runs 8 January - 14 February 2027. All work must be for sale with a 40% commission, artists cover shipping both ways and must supply a prepaid return label. TCA's own timeline labels the 16 November deadline a Wednesday; 16 November 2026 is a Monday, and both the timeline and the CaFE portal give the same date. — Deadline: November 16, 2026. Fee: $35 (first entry) + $5 each additional; membership from $50/year. Prize: $900 in awards + Solo exhibition.

item.title: The Shape of Memory · Indiana University Kokomo
item.description: The IU Kokomo Art Gallery's juried summer exhibition asks artists to treat memory as the foundation of identity and expression rather than simple recollection, sharing their own stories through colour, light and distortion and translating how lived experience has shifted over time. Open to all artists over 18 who reside in the United States; work must be original, completed within the last two years, and works created by artificial intelligence are not eligible. Up to three works, 2D, 3D and video all eligible. The gallery cannot take payment through CaFE: after an entry is received, staff email an invoice from gallery2@iu.edu within roughly three to five business days, and the $25 fee must be paid before the entry is shown to the juror. Photographs and works on paper must arrive framed with a wire for hanging; the gallery walls take 2D pieces up to 9.5 feet tall and 9 feet wide through the doors, with two long walls that can carry pieces up to 25 feet. Accepted work is reproduced in an exhibition catalog. Entries close 2 April 2027, notifications 26 April, work received 18-21 May, exhibition 1 June - 7 July 2027 with a closing reception on 7 July, 4-6pm. The call names no juror. — Deadline: April 2, 2027. Fee: $25 (invoiced by email after entry). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Exhibition Program Open Call 2028–2029 · NARS Foundation
item.description: The New York Art Residency and Studios (NARS) Foundation invites proposals for solo and group exhibitions in 2028 and 2029, for its Main Gallery on the fourth floor and the smaller Project Space on the second, both set among the artists' studios of an industrial building in Sunset Park, Brooklyn. NARS presents 12 to 13 exhibitions a year and reserves both spaces for early-career or underrepresented artists and curators chosen through this annual open call, which is open to new applicants and residency alumni alike. Artists, curators, collectives and cultural producers may propose shows of four to five weeks and are encouraged to activate the space with performances, artist talks and other events; selected applicants are invited to develop their proposals further with NARS providing space, support and resources, and a small honorarium is paid to the selected artist or curator at the end of the exhibition. The applicant - artist or curator - must be US-based, though a US-based curator may include international artists in a group proposal of three to five artists, and proposed artists must have confirmed their interest before the application is submitted. Applicants enrolled in a degree-granting art programme are not eligible, and anyone who has previously exhibited at NARS must wait two full years. One proposal per applicant per open call. NARS is a 501(c)(3) supported in part by public funds from the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs; it cannot cover shipping, and artists should expect to install most of the work themselves. Applications ran 31 August to 21 September 2026, 11:59pm ET; decisions follow three to four weeks later. Materials: a resume, a 500-word proposal and up to ten work samples in image, text, audio or video. — Deadline: September 21, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition + Cash honorarium.

item.title: International Artist Residency 2027 — US-Based Fellowship · NARS Foundation
item.description: The NARS Foundation's International Artist Residency Program supports early- to mid-career artists working across all disciplines with three- and six-month residencies in Sunset Park, Brooklyn, alongside an international cohort. This is the autumn open call for US-based artists, covering 2027 Season I (January-March), Season II (April-June) and the two seasons together. Residents get a 24/7 studio of 250-300 square feet, three to four studio visits a month from curators, critics, art historians and gallerists, weekly A.S.A.P. gatherings, artist talks, panels, screenings and salons, and the season closes with a group exhibition in the NARS gallery and an open-studio event. NARS subsidises the cost for every selected US-based artist through a Partial Fellowship: for 2027 the fellowship is $7,292-$7,792 against a one-season programme fee of $9,962-$10,742, leaving the artist responsible for $2,950-$3,450, payable in full or in monthly instalments. One US-based artist per season also receives a Full Fellowship covering the entire programme fee, awarded by a jury of NARS staff and invited art professionals on artistic quality, level of need, studio practice and likely benefit from the NARS community; applicants must tick the relevant section of the form to be considered. The studio is a workspace only - housing, travel, materials and living costs are the artist's own, and there are no specialist facilities, though residents get access to Materials for the Arts. Photography is explicitly among the practices NARS expects, though it supplies no darkroom or equipment. Open to US-based visual artists with an active professional practice of at least three years, including international artists resident in the US for three years or more; students may apply if their programme ends before the residency starts. Applications ran 31 August to 21 September 2026, 11:59pm ET. Materials: a CV, a 400-word residency proposal, a 300-word bio and up to ten work samples. NARS is a 501(c)(3) supported in part by public funds from the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs. — Deadline: September 21, 2026. Fee: $35 application fee; program fee $2,950–$3,450 per season after the partial fellowship. Prize: Residency + Fellowship.

item.title: Singapore Documentary Festival 2027 — Photography Open Call · Objectifs — Centre for Photography and Film
item.description: The Singapore Documentary Festival, run by Objectifs, is looking for the best documentary photography from Southeast Asia for its 2027 edition. Six projects are selected for a group exhibition at the festival in April 2027; one receives the Truth Seeker Foundation Prize, a cash grant of S$5,000 for a project addressing critical social and environmental issues in the region, and the five runners-up each receive S$1,000. All six get budget return flights and accommodation to attend the opening and programmes in Singapore. Applicants must be from Southeast Asia (practitioners living outside the region may apply), have at least five years of professional photography experience including internships, editorial assignments and freelance work, be able to work in English and own full copyright in the submitted work; one project per applicant. Projects must be documentary and rooted in contemporary social issues in Southeast Asia; completed bodies of work must have concluded within the last five years, and ongoing projects are welcome. Every image must be made with a camera - AI-generated work is not accepted, and AI post-processing tools must not add or remove anything the camera captured. Submit a bio, portrait and CV, a synopsis of up to 250 words, 15 to 30 project images at 2000px on the longest side, and up to three recent projects. Deadline 30 September 2026, 2359hr Singapore time; shortlisted applicants may be contacted in October, selections announced in November, image selection and sequencing with the exhibition team from late November to January, production February-March 2027. The jury is Kelsang Dolma, Maye-E Wong, Amrita Chandradas and Chelsea Chua, alongside a representative of the Truth Seeker Foundation. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: S$5,000 + 5 × S$1,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: The Song of Water — Sutri International Photography Festival 2026 · Museo di Palazzo Doebbing
item.description: The Doebbing Foto Festival's international open call selects the exhibition projects for the second Sutri International Photography Festival, running 21 November 2026 to 24 January 2027 in the hill town of Sutri, north of Rome. The 2026 theme is water, read through the title The Song of Water: the call asks photographers to treat water not as a backdrop but as the centre of a visual narrative - its vital force, the memory of territories, marine and river landscapes, climate change through drought, flood and coastal erosion, the human bond with water, architecture and water management, and the symbolism, spirituality, rites and myths of rebirth and purification. Open to individual photographers, professional and amateur, to photographic collectives and to photography schools, with no limit on age or nationality; every artistic approach from documentary to conceptual is accepted, and work made with AI is not. Each submission is a coherent project of 8 to 15 photographs, JPEG, at least 2500 pixels on the long side, with files named FirstName_LastName_WorkTitle_SequenceNumber; multiple distinct projects may be entered. Three winning projects are shown in full in the official festival circuit and promoted on the festival's website and social channels; other works judged worthy are placed in an off-circuit trail of 1 to 3 images per author in partner venues around the town. Printing and installation costs are covered in full by the organisers for every selected photographer, winners and off-circuit alike. The jury is the festival's artistic direction - Raffaella Canfarini, Vittorio Faggiani and Debora Valentini - with a final juror still to be named. Entries and proof of payment must arrive by 20 October 2026, 11:59pm, emailed to info@doebbingfotofestival.it with a title, captions, a short bio, a project text and the entry form from the site; the fee is paid by bank transfer. — Deadline: October 20, 2026. Fee: €20 (first project) + €15 second + €10 each additional. Prize: Festival exhibition.

item.title: Schoenfeld-Capa Scholarship for Concerned Photography · International Center of Photography
item.description: A full-tuition scholarship created in honour of ICP founder Cornell Capa's idea of Concerned Photography - a practice rooted in empathy, ethical storytelling and social engagement - and of longtime ICP board member Pat Schoenfeld. The award covers the entire $12,500 tuition for ICP's online One-Year Certificate in Documentary Practice: Visual Storytelling, and is open to all domestic and international applicants. Recipients are chosen by ICP's Scholarship Committee on the strength of the application and portfolio, with emphasis on clarity of vision and potential impact in documentary photography. Both the programme application and the scholarship form must be submitted by the 18 October 2026 deadline; the programme application itself carries a $60 fee, so a scholarship recipient's total cost is that fee alone. Scholarships and fellowships cannot be combined - an applicant may receive only one award - and applicants are automatically considered for ICP's merit-based awards through a section inside the programme application. Scholarships are only available to students enrolling in the One-Year Certificate programmes; part-time courses and Open Education workshops are not eligible. ICP is not an accredited institution, so the certificate does not qualify for federal student loans. Applications are made through SlideRoom; results are emailed with the admission decision. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: $60 program application fee. Prize: $12,500 full tuition scholarship.

item.title: MurthyNAYAK Foundation Scholarship · International Center of Photography
item.description: Offered by ICP with support from PhotoSouthAsia, the MurthyNAYAK Foundation Scholarship is a $10,000 tuition award for artists from the South Asia region who show exceptional achievement and potential in photography. Three scholarships are given, each covering $10,000 of the $12,500 tuition for one of ICP's online One-Year Certificate programmes: Curatorial Practice in Photography, Writing and the Photographic Image, or Documentary Practice: Visual Storytelling. Eligibility is limited to applicants from and currently residing in South Asia - Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, the Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka - who demonstrate strong artistic ability, engagement with contemporary photographic practice and a commitment to impactful projects. Selection is based on the same portfolio, curatorial project proposal or writing sample required for the programme application, and both the programme application and the scholarship form must be in by 18 October 2026. The programme application carries a $60 fee. Scholarships cannot be combined, so an applicant may hold only one award, and the scholarships are open only to students enrolling in the One-Year Certificate programmes rather than part-time courses or Open Education workshops. Applications are made through SlideRoom. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: $60 program application fee. Prize: 3 × $10,000 tuition scholarship.

item.title: The Power of Blue · MVA Gallery
item.description: National call for work built around the colour blue at MVA Gallery (Modern Visual Arts) in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania. The gallery invites artists, photographers and sculptors at every level to answer a set of questions about how blue functions in their work: whether it permeates the whole image or sits in small sections, whether it appears in objects, in nature or in abstract design, and whether it is decorative or structural. Blue is framed as a contradictory colour, standing for freedom, imagination, trust and faith on one side and coldness, loneliness and sadness on the other. There is no restriction on subject matter or style, traditional and non-traditional approaches are equally welcome, and all photographic processes are accepted; there is no cutoff date for when the work was made. Open to US residents aged 18 and over. Entry is $35 for three images and $5 for each additional image up to nine. Jurying is by an anonymous rotating committee of artists, gallerists, art reviewers, publishers and academics. Awards are an Art of Distinction award carrying a featured exhibit in the gallery second room, an optional $200 Director Choice award, honourable mentions that come with free entry to a future MVA show, and an annual grand prize of a New York City exhibition opportunity drawn from everyone shown at the gallery during the year. Work must be wired for hanging, no larger than 48 inches framed and under 50 lbs; photographs should be framed in black or white with white or off-white mats if presented traditionally, and plexiglass is preferred over glass for shipped pieces. The gallery takes 30% commission and artists cover shipping both ways. Exhibition runs 28 February to 26 March 2027. — Deadline: September 29, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $200 + NYC exhibition.

item.title: Creating Collages · MVA Gallery
item.description: National call for collage and collage-like work at MVA Gallery (Modern Visual Arts) in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, with photomontage and digital collage named explicitly alongside mixed media, assemblage and decoupage. The gallery is interested in the juxtaposition of painted and photographic imagery with coloured paper, printed text, fabric and found objects, and in work that is two-dimensional or three-dimensional, structured or floating, serious, humorous, irreverent or satirical. Any subject matter is welcome. Artists, photographers, printmakers and sculptors at every level may enter and all photographic processes are accepted; there is no cutoff date for when the work was made. Open to US residents aged 18 and over. Entry is $35 for three images and $5 for each additional image up to nine. Jurying is by an anonymous rotating committee of artists, gallerists, art reviewers, publishers and academics. Awards are an Art of Distinction award carrying a featured exhibit in the gallery second room, an optional $200 Director Choice award, honourable mentions that come with free entry to a future MVA show, and an annual grand prize of a New York City exhibition opportunity drawn from everyone shown at the gallery during the year. Work must be wired for hanging, no larger than 48 inches framed and under 45 lbs; photographs should be framed in black or white with white or off-white mats if presented traditionally, and plexiglass is preferred over glass for shipped pieces. The gallery takes 30% commission and artists cover shipping both ways. Exhibition runs 28 February to 26 March 2027. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $200 + NYC exhibition.

item.title: 2027 Artist in Residence · Great Basin National Park
item.description: Free open call for three 2027 artist residencies at Great Basin National Park in eastern Nevada, run with the Great Basin National Park Foundation, which funds the programme. Artists are surrounded by the park from the 13,063-foot summit of Wheeler Peak to the depths of Lehman Caves, with wilderness solitude and renowned dark-sky stargazing. Applicants choose the seasons they want to be considered for: a winter residency of two to three weeks in January or February with park housing (a furnished private bedroom in a shared living space with kitchen, bathroom and laundry), a summer residency of two to three weeks in July or August that is a camping residency with gear supplied by the Foundation, or a fall residency of two to three weeks in September or October, which can be timed to overlap the park Astronomy Festival. The two surfaces disagree about the fall term: the park's own page lists it as a housed residency on the same terms as winter, and notes that fall and winter residencies with NPS housing require a background check, while the CaFÉ prospectus calls it a camping-only residence — confirm with the coordinator before choosing that season. The park is remote: the nearest town, Baker, has few or no amenities and Ely is 60 to 70 miles away; cell service is limited and campgrounds have no internet or electricity. Open to visual artists, literary artists, musicians and other creative media artists residing anywhere, with one of the three places held for a regional artist living and working in Nevada or Utah. Each resident becomes an NPS volunteer, presents one public programme in the park, delivers a virtual programme within six months and a digital portfolio within three months, and donates one physical piece plus a digital representation to the Foundation within a year under a deed of gift, which may be displayed in the park for up to three years. The digital portfolio will not be monetised and exclusive rights are not requested; artists are always credited. Applications are reviewed by jury panels of past participants, subject-matter experts, local community members and park staff, and selected artists are announced by press release in January. — Deadline: October 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 2-3 week residency with park lodging or campsite.

item.title: Florida’s Natural Beauty 2026 · Audubon of Martin County
item.description: Juried photography contest and exhibition presented by Audubon of Martin County and hosted by the Historical Society of Martin County at the Elliott Museum in Stuart, Florida. Open to all amateur and professional photographers residing in the US; every photograph and video must have been taken in Florida. Six categories: Birds, Wildlife, Flora/Landscape, Creative, Video and Cell Phone Photography. Up to seven images or videos may be entered per category, each image in one category only, at $25 per uploaded photograph for non-members and $20 for Audubon of Martin County members. Only global adjustments are allowed outside the Creative category, and the use of AI is not permitted in the Creative category. Camera-trap images are disqualified, recognisable individuals need a signed release, and photographs previously entered into an Audubon of Martin County contest are not eligible. Awards are Best in Show $300, and in each category first $200, second $100 and third $50, with honourable mentions at the judges discretion; judging is blind, by a panel of three independent photography experts. This is not a digital-only exhibit: accepted images must be supplied as museum-quality framed, canvas, acrylic or metal prints, minimum 8 inches on the short side and no more than 20 by 24 inches including the frame, wired for hanging. Notification 11 December 2026; opening reception and awards at the Elliott Museum 21 January 2027; exhibition on view daily 22 January to 25 February 2027. Photographers keep copyright, with limited permission granted for archival, publicity and promotional use. Sales are split 75% to the artist and 25% to the Museum. Out-of-area entrants may ship accepted prints prepaid round trip. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: $25 per photo (non-members) / $20 members. Prize: $300 Best in Show + museum exhibition.

item.title: Luis Ferreira Alves Photography Award 2026
item.description: Second edition of the biennial Luis Ferreira Alves International Photography Competition — A Contemporary Look at Architecture, a free award founded in tribute to the Portuguese architectural photographer and run from Porto by Cityscopio with Porto City Council, the Faculty of Architecture of the University of Porto and Casa da Arquitectura. Open to photographers of all nationalities, working individually or collectively, with a series of 9 to 11 images engaging a single work of architecture, a group of works or a broader architectural context; analogue or digital, colour or black and white, plus a project statement of up to 2,000 characters. First prize is EUR 10,000, second EUR 4,000 and third a EUR 1,500 photographic-equipment voucher; the 2026 edition adds a Portuguese Emerging Photography Award (a further EUR 1,500 voucher) for Portuguese artists. Up to ten finalists, plus any special mentions, are shown in the official exhibition and published in the catalogue, and judging is blind through the platform. Generative AI is not permitted. Submissions open 25 September 2026 and close 1 January 2027 at 23:59 mainland Portugal time; the first international edition drew 1,495 entries from 99 countries. — Deadline: January 1, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: €10,000 / €4,000 / €1,500 voucher + Exhibition + Publication.

item.title: Framed: Shadow and Light · Black Box Gallery
item.description: Juried group photography show at Black Box Gallery in Portland on shadow and light — dramatic shadows and patterns in black and white, ethereal and moody shadow and texture in colour, and the range of ways contemporary photographers read the two together. Juror Todd Johnson, the gallery's founder and director, selects 26 photographs for the gallery walls and a further 50 for the online gallery annex; all 76 appear in a catalogue published through Blurb. The gallery prints, mats and frames every exhibited work at no cost to the photographer, using an Epson archival inkjet setup and its own 18 × 24 inch frames, and keeps exhibition prints in its flat files for two years to show to collectors and curators. Artists retain all rights to the file and the print, no print is sold without the photographer's prior consent and a signed authentication document, and work does not have to be offered for sale; if it is, the split is 50/50. Entry is $40 for up to five photographs, submitted by email after paying through PayPal. Open to all photographers worldwide, amateur and professional. Exhibition runs November 1–25, 2026. — Deadline: October 9, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: Gallery exhibition + Catalog.

item.title: Pride Photo 2027
item.description: Free annual international contest from the Amsterdam non-profit Pride Photo, open to photographers worldwide of all ages, backgrounds and levels, for work that explores LGBTQIA+ lives, identities and visual languages. Two categories: STORIES, a project series of 3 to 15 images, and SINGLE IMAGES, up to five standalone works; two projects per application and multiple applications allowed. Documentary photography, portraiture, collage and photographic intervention are all welcome. Selected photographers receive EUR 500 for each work included in the Pride Photo Exhibition 2027, which opens publicly in Amsterdam and then travels nationally and internationally from spring 2027 to spring 2028, with credited features across Pride Photo's print and digital platforms. The 2027 jury is chaired by Supranav Dash with Katy Hundertmark, Papa De, Marit Lena Hermmann and Marwan Kaboor. Any use of AI must be declared and explained, and images created entirely through generative AI are not accepted; Pride Photo's published reasoning is that images representing LGBTQIA+ lives should be grounded in lived reality. Copyright stays with the photographer. Submissions close 31 October 2026 at 23:59 CET; winners are announced in June 2027. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €500 per selected work + Exhibition.

item.title: Carroll Harris Simms National Black Art Competition and Exhibition · African American Museum, Dallas
item.description: Biennial national competition and exhibition at the African American Museum in Dallas, open to Black artists residing in the United States. The museum began the competition in 1976 to build its collection and give Black artists a venue, and named it in 1999 for Carroll Harris Simms, co-founder of the Texas Southern University art department. A $1,000 award goes to one artist in each of six categories — painting, sculpture, mixed media, drawing, printmaking and photography — and one of the six category winners is chosen Best in Show, which carries a solo exhibition at the museum within the following two years; the Best in Show artist agrees to donate a work from that show to the museum's permanent collection. Entry is $25, with one to four images per work in JPEG at 300 dpi and a maximum 5 MB per file, plus an artist statement and current biography; sculpture entries take one to four views.
