Up to three separate applications are allowed. AI-generated art and photography are not accepted. Entry deadline November 20, 2026, with selection notifications November 23–27 and accepted work delivered by January 17, 2027. — Deadline: November 20, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: $1,000 per category + Solo exhibition.

item.title: 43rd Five State Photography Competition & Exhibition · Hays Arts Council
item.description: Annual regional fine-art photography competition run by the Hays Arts Council in Kansas and open to photographers living in Kansas, Nebraska, Missouri, Oklahoma and Colorado. Now in its 43rd year, the exhibition is the anchor of the Winter Art Walk and opens to the public each December. Any photographic process and any subject is eligible, provided the work was made in the last three years and has not been in a previous Five State exhibition; each photograph is entered and judged in one of three categories — Nature, People or Open. Juror Elise Kirk, Associate Professor of Photography and chair of the Department of Visual Art at the University of Kansas, selects 100 photographs for exhibition and awards $1,500 in cash across the three categories. Entry is $25 for the first two photographs and $7.50 for each of up to two more, paid by card or by cheque. Files are JPEG only, no larger than 30 MB, at least 1,200 pixels on the long side, in a 4:5 aspect ratio, and selected work is printed by the photographer at 8 × 10 inches; the council mats and frames every accepted print itself. Entries and payments are due October 23, 2026, acceptances go out by November 4, and the exhibition runs December 5, 2026 to January 31, 2027. — Deadline: October 23, 2026. Fee: $25 (2 photos) + $7.50 each additional. Prize: $1,500 in cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Companions · L.A. Photo Curator
item.description: Open call from L.A. Photo Curator on the animals we live alongside — the pets that greet us, wait for us and quietly become companions rather than animals we care for. Juried by Laurie Freitag, who founded L.A. Photo Curator eleven years ago. Every entrant is included in the online group exhibition with an artist statement, biography and website link, and the first-place photographer receives a solo online exhibition, an online article with a Q&A drawing on the juror's responses, and their image on the L.A. Photo Curator splash page for a month; selected work is also considered for the platform's Top 40 Images of the Year and its Photographer of the Year. One participating photographer is invited to serve as guest juror alongside Freitag on a future call. Entry is $25 for either three or six images, paid through PayPal and then emailed as a ZIP of JPEGs at 1024 pixels on the long side. Five per cent of entry fees goes to a charity chosen by the winner. Open to all photographers worldwide, amateur and professional. Deadline September 27, 2026. — Deadline: September 27, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: Solo online exhibition.

item.title: The Chico Review 2027 · Charcoal Book Club
item.description: Juried application to the eleventh Chico Review, the photobook retreat organised by Charcoal Book Club at Chico Hot Springs Resort in Paradise Valley, Montana, March 15–21, 2027. Eighty photographers are selected by jury from open application and spend seven days with more than twenty-five photographers, bookmakers, gallerists, curators and photobook publishers; each attendee receives ten 20-minute portfolio reviews plus artist lectures, panel discussions, peer reviews and evening programming. One attending photographer is awarded the Charcoal Publishing Prize, and their project is published and distributed worldwide by Charcoal Book Club. Six merit scholarships are awarded on the strength of the submitted work — one full tuition ($5,450), two half tuition ($2,675) and three partial ($1,500) — with academic discounts and limited need-based scholarships also available on acceptance. Applicants submit a cohesive body of work; there is no theme. 2027 speakers include Paul Graham, Barbara Bosworth, Daniel Arnold, Rena Effendi, JH Engström, Paul D'Amato, Emma Hardy and Hannah Modigh. Application fee $25 for Charcoal Book Club members, $50 otherwise, rising to a $65 late entry fee in late November. Attendance, if selected, is $5,450 tuition and board plus lodging at $70–$250 a night. — Deadline: November 29, 2026. Fee: $50 non-members / $25 members / $65 late entry after Nov 23. Prize: Book publication + 6 merit scholarships ($5,450 / $2,675 / $1,500).

item.title: Daisy Lane: Print & Book Artist Residency 2027 · Bainbridge Island Museum of Art
item.description: Free-to-apply residency at Daisy Lane, the Bainbridge Island Museum of Art's new print and book arts studio minutes from the museum, for artists working in book arts, letterpress, screenprinting, Risograph and related print forms — which includes photographers making artists' books and photobooks. Two residents are in place at any time, one local and one travelling, each for two to four weeks, with studio access from 8am to 10pm daily and easy access to the museum, its events and the Cynthia Sears Artists' Books Collection. The studio was equipped in part with presses and equipment acquired from Paper Hammer and Marquand Books, the letterpress, printmaking and book design studio in Tieton, Washington. Selection is on conceptual creativity, technical knowledge and familiarity with at least one of the studio's processes; familiarity need not be advanced, and orientation and instruction on the equipment are provided. Applicants submit contact information, a project proposal, an artist biography and five to ten work samples. Applications for 2027 residents open October 1, 2026 and close December 1, 2026. There is no application fee; CaFÉ offers an optional $25 support payment. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: Free (optional $25 support fee). Prize: Residency (2–4 weeks).

item.title: Long River Review 2027 — Art & Photography
item.description: Free open submissions for the art and photography section of Long River Review, the University of Connecticut's literary and arts magazine, now on its twenty-ninth print issue and run by an MFA-student editorial board. The magazine welcomes all art mediums including photography, illustration, printmaking, painting, comics, drawing and mixed media; the submission limit is five to ten pieces with a 150-word artist statement explaining the work. Files should be TIFF or EPS at 350 dpi, 5.75 inches minimum to 8 inches maximum width, in CMYK for colour and greyscale for black and white. Only unpublished work is accepted; simultaneous submissions are fine if you notify the editors. Accepted contributors give first North American serial rights, after which rights revert, and receive two copies of the issue their work appears in; the magazine is not in a position to pay contributors. Art submitted by UConn students is additionally considered for the Gloriana Gill Art Awards and the Long River Art Award. AI-generated visual content is not published and the editors describe the review process they follow if a submission is suspected. Reading period September 15 to December 15, with decisions by the end of April. — Deadline: December 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication (print).

item.title: The Fine Odd · Hand Fetish Projects
item.description: Rolling open call for The Fine Odd, a fine-art artbook from independent arthouse Hand-Fetish-Projects, published in two separate volumes — 01 Photography and 02 Visual Art & Print-Based Work. The photography volume is open to conceptual, documentary, staged, experimental, analogue, digital, fashion and manipulated work, submitted as a single image or as part of a series. There is no fixed theme: artists respond to “odd” as a condition rather than a subject, and 18+ themes, sexuality and fetish are welcome but not required. Selected artists receive two dedicated spreads, 2–5 works, bespoke layout with full credits, permanent archiving, a complimentary digital copy and discounted print copies. Artists retain full copyright; HFP takes a non-exclusive licence that also covers derivative retail products such as prints and postcard sets, with revenue split 55% to the artist on single-artist items. $15 for three pieces, $25 for five. No deadline is published — submissions are reviewed on a rolling basis. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: $15–$25. Prize: Publication (print).

item.title: LIGHT · California Art League
item.description: A live juried exhibition on the theme of Light, presented by the California Art League at bG Gallery in Bergamot Station, Santa Monica, and hung there from 3 to 18 November 2026. Om Navon Bleicher, who founded bG Gallery in 2009 and directs it, is the sole juror and picks both the show and the awards from the digital images submitted. Awards are $800 Best of Show, $500 first place, $200 second place, $100 third place, three honourable mentions and the Theodore Herman Award for Photography. The League - founded in 1948 as the Valley Artists Guild by the sculptor Henry Van Wolf and renamed in 2012 - says painters, sculptors, photographers and collage artists are welcome, and this call accepts drawing, painting, photographs, digital art, mixed media, collage and sculpture; no performance art or AI is accepted. Work must be original and created by the artist from conception to completion, and must not have been shown in a CAL exhibit before. The call is open to CAL members and non-members alike: one or two entries cost $35 for members with dues current and $55 for non-members, the $20 difference being a one-time charge that also gives the new artist a discounted CAL membership; further works are $5 each up to a total of six. There is a 30-inch maximum frame width for wall art. Entries close 11 October at midnight PST and artists are notified on 19 October. Accepted work must be hand delivered to the gallery on 2 November; all work must be for sale and must not be offered for sale anywhere else until 30 days after the show closes, with bG Gallery taking a 50% commission on sales in that period. The opening reception and awards presentation is on Saturday 7 November, with an artists' talk on 15 November and pick-up on 19 November. — Deadline: October 11, 2026. Fee: $55 non-members / $35 members for 1-2 works, $5 each additional (max 6). Prize: $800 Best of Show + $500/$200/$100 places + Exhibition.
